rq-mg-01.front: Four ways animals move in BC?
rq-mg-01.back: Long distance (ducks, geese), up and down (mule deer, elk, moose, dusky grouse), short shifts (white tails), stay home (quail, chukar, ruffed grouse).

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 320" role="img" aria-label="Four cards. Long distance migrants: ducks and geese. Elevational, up and down: mule deer, elk, moose and dusky grouse. Short shifts along or across valleys: white tailed deer. Residents that stay home: quail, chukar and ruffed grouse.">

rq-mg-05.front: Do mule deer change routes each year?
rq-mg-05.back: No. Most choose nearly the same path both ways (85%).

rq-mg-06.front: When do collared mule deer return to winter range?
rq-mg-06.back: October to November; one year nearly all by mid October (85%).

rq-mg-13.back: They move to open valley water and the coast (65%).

rq-mg-14.back: Move from open breeding areas into dense conifers, usually uphill (70%).
